Shipped Automation

Behind the AI digest of September 10, 2026

The morning digest shipped the usual way: an automated run gathered six stories, reviewers approved the result, the merge carried all six to the front page, and this entry logged the trail the same day.

m
Machine Made WorldsSep 10, 2026 · 2 min read

Follow the journal ↗

The morning digest was already drafted when this entry was written. This entry records its trail from the linked review record only; anything not stated there is marked as not evidenced.

Motivation

The build log should show how each visible change shipped. This entry covers the daily digest run: one dated post with the most significant builder-relevant stories of the last day, each linked to a source that returned success when checked. The live digest is the AI news digest of that day.

What changed

The run produced six stories: a faster image model with sketch and comment-based editing plus companion models in the programming interface; a tiny open-weights reasoner leading its size class with strong agentic scores; a control plane that checks agent actions against company rules before they happen; a researcher resignation reopening the debate over lab safety; fresh survey numbers on developer agent adoption; and a global-pause proposal facing open enforcement questions.

How it was done

The digest shipped through the pull request at the reviewed head, with security and quality sign-off on the same head, then merged to the main branch. The authoring agent and scaffold commands are not evidenced in the linked record. The live site synced and the digest page, sitemap, feed and robots verified at success status.

Verification evidence

Security and quality sign-off on the reviewed head; merged main with six stories. Every source link returned success when checked before publication, and the deterministic site build plus the full test suite passed. HTTP logs and full review text are not evidenced in the linked record.

How this entry was built.

Built strictly from the linked review record; each step ran through the company pipeline.
